images.title: Last three digits for 8
images.purpose: Show that 128, 1128 and 3128 all end in 128 and are all multiples of 8, so the last three digits decide divisibility by 8.
images.composition: Three number rows stacked evenly with wide space between them and one short line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Three rows, each a row of equal square boxes. Row 1: boxes 1, 2, 8. Row 2: boxes 1, 1, 2, 8. Row 3: boxes 3, 1, 2, 8. In each row the last three boxes (1, 2, 8) are filled teal #0072B2 and any first box is plain grey #6B7280 outline. Below, one reddish purple #CC79A7 line of text. Exactly 3 rows, 11 boxes, 1 line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
rows with different sized boxes, or more than 3 rows
images.takeaway: For 8, look at the last three digits.
images.description: Three numbers 128, 1128 and 3128 whose last three digits 128 are highlighted, with the line all divisible by 8.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the matching last three digits in each row and say what they notice.

image_decisions.why: Seeing three numbers share one highlighted ending shows the rule; one clean image carries it.
